source_caption:
One of the greatest shots in cinema history! 

Once Upon a Time in America (1984), directed by Sergio Leone, is a long, emotional crime drama about friendship, ambition, and regret. It follows David “Noodles” Aaronson, played by Robert De Niro, as he looks back on his life growing up in New York’s Jewish ghetto and rising through the world of organized crime with his childhood friends.

The story moves between different time periods, showing them as kids, young gangsters during Prohibition, and later as older men dealing with the consequences of their past. At the center is Noodles’ complicated friendship with Max, full of loyalty, jealousy, and betrayal.

More than just a gangster movie, it’s really about memory and how the past stays with you. It explores how choices, especially the bad ones, shape your whole life. By the end, it feels less like a crime story and more like a bittersweet reflection on lost time, broken friendships, and the cost of chasing power.

source_details.synopsis: Once Upon a Time in America (Italian: C'era una volta in America) is a 1984 epic crime film based on Harry Grey's semi-autobiographical 1952 novel The Hoods. Directed by Sergio Leone from a screenplay he co-wrote with Leonardo Benvenuti, Piero De Bernardi, Enrico Medioli, Franco Arcalli and Franco Ferrini, the film stars Robert De Niro, James Woods, Elizabeth McGovern, Joe Pesci, Burt Young, Tuesday Weld and Treat Williams. The film is an Italian–American venture produced by The Ladd Company, Embassy International Pictures, PSO Enterprises and Rafran Cinematografica, and distributed by Warner Bros. It chronicles the lives of best friends David "Noodles" Aaronson and Maximilian "Max" Bercovic
